title: Build Your First d3m0n App
description: Set up the d3c toolchain, create a native app, and build a .d3m0n executable.

courses.name: Set up the d3c SDK
courses.description: Install the compiler and create a project from the official template.

activities.title: Apps for the current d3m0n OS
activities.value: The current d3m0n OS app toolchain is d3c, the C++ compiler and SDK included in the d3m0n_os repository. It builds native app executables with the .d3m0n extension. The older layout and source lessons described a different app system and do not apply to this version.

activities.title: Install d3c
activities.value: On a Linux development machine, clone the OS repository and install the compiler for your user. The compiler Makefile builds d3c and installs its SDK headers and project template. Add the printed install directory to PATH if the installer says it is not already available.

git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/d3m0n-project/d3m0n_os.git
cd d3m0n_os/compiler
make INSTALL_FOR_EVERYONE=0 install
export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/com.ares"
d3c init HelloD3m0n
cd HelloD3m0n

The commands above follow the current compiler Makefile: it installs to ~/com.ares for a user install. If you open a new terminal, add export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/com.ares" to your shell profile so that d3c stays available.

courses.name: Explore the starter project
courses.description: Understand the template entry point, metadata, and window code.

activities.title: Project structure
activities.value: The generated project contains a Makefile, icon.ico, and a src directory. The Makefile compiles every C++ source file under src with d3c and writes one executable named after the project. Start by reading src/main.cpp and the example window under src/windows.

activities.title: App entry point and metadata
activities.value: The template calls APP_INFO(name, version, author, description, icon) to embed app details. Its main function creates a window and passes it to Application::run(window). Use the SDK headers in compiler/sdk/lib and the template as the working example for available UI classes and events.

Keep the template's SDK includes, metadata macro, and C-linkage main entry point while you make your first changes. Check the example window and SDK headers before using an API; the old web Academy's layout controls and scripting syntax belong to a retired system.

questions.question: Where does the starter project put C++ source files?

courses.name: Build and install your app
courses.description: Compile the project, then place the executable where the OS launcher can find it.

activities.title: Compile a .d3m0n executable
activities.value: From the project directory, run make export. The template Makefile invokes d3c and places the executable in the current directory; for the project above, the output is HelloD3m0n.d3m0n. You can also compile an individual C++ source with d3c, but the template Makefile is the simplest way to build a multi-file app.

activities.title: Run it on d3m0n OS
activities.value: Copy the finished .d3m0n file to the device's /apps directory. The OS launcher scans that directory (and its category subdirectories) for .d3m0n executables; open the launcher and select your app. The template's Application::run starts its main window. For a repeatable development workflow, add your app to the OS repository's applications tree using the existing app Makefile pattern; make export builds those apps into an OS image.

You can try the app on real hardware after following Getting Started. To build and boot the OS in QEMU, see the OS repository instructions. The current app template does not document a standalone simulator workflow, so validate against a device or the repository's supported emulator setup.
